items.content_html:
Summary

Marks InputDeviceInfo as unsupported by firefox.

Test results and supporting details

Noticed issue by trying this jsfiddle, which is simply const info = MediaDeviceInfo, and results in InputDeviceInfo is not defined in current Firefox.

Tried to find a few citable sources to substantiate the claim, here's what I found on searchfox.org:

MediaDevices-enumerateDevices.https.html.ini:

[InputDeviceInfo is supported]
  expected: FAIL

idlharness.https.window.js.ini:

  [InputDeviceInfo interface: existence and properties of interface prototype object]
    expected: FAIL

moz.build:

Doesn't include InputDeviceInfo.idl, only MediaDeviceInfo.idl, which doesn't contain InputDeviceInfo

Related issues

  • fixes: #27495
items.title: Indicate `InputDeviceInfo` is not available in Firefox

items.content_html:
Summary

Chrome 139 adds support for the corner-shape property, and its related shorthands and longhands. See https://chromestatus.com/feature/5357329815699456.

The properties have already been added to BCD by the collector, but the types that it can take as values have not.

This PR adds data for the types.

Note that I have included two data points for superellipse() — one for the function itself, and one for the use of superellipse() as a <corner-shape-value>. I thought this was a good idea in case superellipse() has more parameter options added, or is used as a possible value for other properties in the future.

Test results and supporting details

Related issues

items.content_html:
Summary

As discussed in Mozilla Bug 1316857 comment 18, the concept of "same script" is vague and likely inaccurate.

Additionally, to determine script-closeability, browsers switched from 'has an opener' to 'was opened by script' and that might be useful to note.

Test results and supporting details

https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1316857#c18

Related issues

#9492

My perception is these notes are usually quite short. Script-closeability also depends on the session history, so something like "Before Chrome 95, scripts could only close windows that had an opener" would be incorrect. I tried to omit this detail, but am unsure whether that made my phrasing too awkward. We could remove the notes entirely. An alternative phrasing might be "Before Chrome 95, whether a window could be closed by script depended on having an opener, not on whether it was created by web content."
items.title: Revise notes for historic window.close() behavior
